title: California bands compared with New Orleans style
summary: Williams says the Los Angeles Black and Tan band tried to play like New Orleans bands, and recalls who went west before and after him.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, I think I just remember the drummer there. Was it Ben Varders, the drummer with the Black and Tan? Did you ever hear him? Who? Varders. Varder. I think it was Ben Varders. What kind of music was out there in the local bands in California? Was it anything like the style of the Marlene's band? No, it wasn't. That's why we taken so. That's what I wondered.
That's why we taken. See, now the Black and Tan band was the best band there, you know, see. Trying to play like us, you know. But after we went there, then.
They didn't really have the style. No, they didn't have it at all. No, they didn't have the style. We wrapped it up when we went there.

Yeah. Yes, indeed. But Buddy P.T. and I believe Charlie Love was out there before us, wasn't he? Did he ever tell you? I believe, no, not Charlie. Frankie Duesen went out. Frankie Duesen? Charlie Love didn't go with him? I don't know. Must have been Buddy P.T. Buddy and Frankie Duesen. Oh, Buddy and Frankie. When I heard that, yeah, I heard they went out there.

And Joe Oliver didn't go out until about 1921. He took his band out. Yeah, I was back here. You were back there. He stayed out there a good while, didn't he? Quite a while in San Francisco and then stopped in Los Angeles a while.
There's a lot of bands in California, a lot of people out there. Yeah, oh, yes. I was out there in October.
